newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile February exports rise, imports down slightly.
newsitem.headline: Chile February exports rise, imports down slightly.

text.p: Chile's trade surplus swelled in February to $139 million as the result of a rise in exports and a slight fall in imports with the exception of oil imports, said the Central Bank in its fortnightly report.
February's figures bring the trade surplus in the first two months of the year to $172 million compared with an even trade balance in the January-February period 1996.
Exports rose three percent to $1.3 billion, mainly as a result of a 3.4 percent increase in copper exports despite lower prices, said the report.
Other top exports, including fresh fruit and fishmeal, fell four percent because of lower international prices.
Imports fell 0.7 percent last month on February 1996, in spite of a 27 percent increase in oil imports.
Intermediate goods imports were down 0.5 percent, while capital goods imports dropped 0.3 percent.
Consumer goods imports fell 1.7 percent, which "is consistent with the process of deceleration which this variable has shown in recent months," the report said.
